title: Nut Roast
subtitle: Hearty mixed nut roast with herbs and vegetables
excerpt: Walnuts, cashews, and hazelnuts combined with onion, celery, herbs, and cheese, baked in a loaf tin until golden. A proper centrepiece for a vegetarian Sunday lunch.

recipe.sourceNotes: Nut roast became the default British vegetarian Sunday lunch alternative during the 1970s and 1980s, boosted by the Cranks cookbook and the growing whole-food movement. A well-made nut roast is firm enough to slice, moist enough not to crumble, and deeply savoury from the combination of nuts, cheese, and herbs. The key is the right ratio of nuts to binding ingredients: eggs and breadcrumbs hold it together while the nuts provide the body.

content.text: Process the nuts briefly: you want roughly chopped pieces with some texture rather than a fine paste. Line the loaf tin with baking paper with enough overhang to lift the roast out. The nut roast can be assembled up to a day ahead and refrigerated unbaked.

Heat the oven to 180 C / fan 160 C / gas 4. Line a 900 g loaf tin with baking paper. Melt the butter in a frying pan over medium heat. Fry the onion and celery for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Leave to cool slightly.
Pulse the nuts in a food processor until roughly chopped, with some larger pieces remaining. Tip into a large bowl.
Add the cooked onion and celery, eggs, breadcrumbs, cheese, tomato puree, thyme, rosemary, soy sauce, salt, and pepper. Mix well. The mixture should hold together when pressed.

Press the mixture into the lined loaf tin. Smooth the top. Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until firm to the touch and golden on top. Leave in the tin for 5 minutes before lifting out. Slice and serve with gravy, roast potatoes, and greens.
